gaps.sentence: My grandmother goes to ___ church every morning before work.
gaps.explanation: 'Go to church' (as worshipper) takes no article; 'the church' would mean the building.

gaps.sentence: The car crashed into a wall at ___ speed of 90 km/h.
gaps.explanation: 'At a speed of…' — 'a' is part of this fixed phrase.

gaps.sentence: She's studying history at ___ University of Vienna.
gaps.explanation: University names with of-phrases take the: the University of Vienna.

gaps.sentence: ___ few days he had left were spent packing.
___ Smith family have lived in this street since 1990.
gaps.explanation: 'The Smith family' — the whole family takes 'the'.
'MA' is pronounced /em/, starting with a vowel sound, so 'an MA'.

gaps.sentence: We had ___ lunch at a bistro near the cathedral.
gaps.explanation: Names of meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) take no article when used generally.

gaps.sentence: My grandfather was ___ engineer during the war.
gaps.explanation: 'An engineer' — 'engineer' begins with a vowel sound.
